result.topic_en: Riemann discusses characterizing a system of functions $(y_1,\dots,y_n)$ of a class by a symbol showing its branch-point exponents and substitution, and shows that between any n+1 systems of the same class there is a homogeneous linear equation with entire functions of x as coefficients, the coefficients being proportional to determinants.

$$a_0 y_2 + a_1 y_2^{(1)} + \dots + a_n y_2^{(n)} = 0$$
$$\dots\dots$$

items.english: It is now not hard to prove that between any n+1 systems belonging to the same class there holds a linear homogeneous equation with entire functions of x as coefficients.

items.english: It is obvious here that every system can be regarded as a special case of infinitely many others, in which the corresponding exponents are partly or entirely different.
